task.description: WF-02 Step 1 (CODE-DESIGNER) for run-id WF02-REQ019-20260816: produce the design artefact for REQ-019 (tenant<->realm binding, OIDC-12/ADP-04b equivalent) — resolveTenantByRealm/resolveRealmByTenant-equivalent functions, the tenant create/update changesets (one-to-one binding enforcement, idp_realm_id immutability, default-tenant pinning), and the realm-ownership guard function, all landing on Letflow.Identity/Letflow.Identity.Tenant alongside REQ-018's already-merged provision_oidc_user/3. result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req019-tenant-realm-binding.md covering: (1) resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and resolve_realm_by_tenant/1 on Letflow.Identity, exact @specs and query mechanism against Letflow.Identity.Tenant, with resolve_realm_by_tenant/1's {:ok, nil} case flagged as a deliberate divergence from realm_tenant_binding.zig's literal null-handling; (2) create_changeset/3 and update_changeset/2 on Letflow.Identity.Tenant (schema-module placement, matching REQ-018's Approval/User precedent), with unique_constraint(:idp_realm_id, name: :tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index) surfacing REQ-015's existing partial index as a clean {:error, changeset} (INV-8); (3) idp_realm_id immutability enforced structurally by update_changeset/2 omitting the field from cast/3 entirely, with an explicit no-rotation-function decision; (4) default-tenant pinning via a reserved slug marker ("bpm-default") rather than a reserved UUID (no seed file exists in this repo, confirmed by search, so 'seeded' is specified as a TEST-DESIGNER-constructed fixture, not a migration); (5) verify_realm_ownership/2 realm-ownership guard with all four edge cases specified (match/mismatch/tenant-not-found/nil-realm-bound) and a re-query-the-DB trust-boundary decision (does not trust a caller-passed realm, since a guard trusting the value under test would be a no-op); (6) all new functions placed on Letflow.Identity (context) / Letflow.Identity.Tenant (schema changesets), no new files; (7) error-type composition with REQ-018 stated explicitly — new functions do not extend provisioning_error(), but :realm_tenant_mismatch is reused verbatim as REQ-018's design already reserved. Six open questions flagged explicitly (oidc_mode config-key source, slug mutability, whether a real seed file should exist, DB-exception wrapping policy parity with REQ-018's own OQ-4, resolve_realm_by_tenant/1's nil-handling divergence, provisioning_error() naming once REQ-021 composes). INV-1/INV-7/INV-8 explicitly assessed in a dedicated section for SECURITY-REVIEWER. Full acceptance-criteria traceability table included. No implementation code present — verified by grep for defmodule/def/case-do patterns, zero matches.
